# Feature x framework

<!-- Generated by `make matrix-page` (python -m tests.matrix.page) from the test matrix:
     do not edit; tests/unit/test_docs.py fails when this page and the matrix differ. -->

Which feature works with which framework, as the test matrix (`tests/matrix`) tests it.
This page is written from the matrix's own tables and a test fails when the two differ,
so it cannot claim what is not tested. `make matrix` runs every test counted here (CI
runs it on every change; `build/matrix.md` is the result of a run).

A test is one feature on one framework, in one of the 7 ways a run is driven
(`run`, `stream`, `worker`, `elsewhere`, `schedule`, `agui`, `a2a`), under one selection of what is on (everything,
nothing, the feature's needs alone, each of them turned off with `without=`).

- **yes n**: n tests run the feature on that framework, every mode
- **partly n (k)**: n tests; the modes left out do not apply, for reason k below
- **no (k)**: the feature does not apply to that framework, for reason k below
- **waits on G..**: the tests run and must fail until the gap or bug named closes

## Reasons

1. nothing is streamed: no listener in this mode
2. a function target has no model: your code calls the tools itself
3. ReAct's approvals are the harness's own (F32)
4. the graph's in-memory checkpointer is the pausing process's own
5. a scheduled run's pause is the queued run's (covered by worker)
6. a function target has no framework approvals
7. G5 (can_use_tool, session resume) concerns Claude's built-in tools, which the scripted CLI cannot call: the live suite's
8. a function target runs its own calls (asyncio.gather)
9. the scripted Claude CLI calls one tool at a time (the real CLI's concurrency is unverified)
10. a function target runs its own calls
11. native: the graph runs a turn's calls its own way (N3); HarnessTools orders the writes (ReAct has it)
12. native: the framework runs a turn's calls its own way (N3)
13. a function target gets the whole result: it has no context to fill
14. native: add FilesystemMiddleware(tools=['read_file']) to create_agent (ReAct and Deep Agents have it by default)
15. a function target has no model context
16. native: ContextEditingMiddleware and Deep Agents' summarization, which ReAct is built with (Deep Agents has its summarization by default; add them to create_agent)
17. the framework keeps its own context (its compaction, its trimming)
18. checked by F41f: a function target reads agent.context
19. checked by F41 (what the model is sent)
20. a function target calls the memory tools like any other (F43)
21. the AG-UI surface is its own mode
22. the A2A surface is its own mode
23. schedules are their own mode
24. queued runs are the worker modes
25. no model call the harness can hook (a function makes none; the CLI's are its own)
26. a surface takes no per-run option: the agent's own (h.wrap) applies
27. a queue order is a queued run's: start and schedule take it
28. no framework run call: framework_options= is refused
29. by design: in Way 2 your code runs the agent, so its stream and events are its framework's own; the harness numbers the events of the runs it runs (Way 1)
30. Way 2 recipes use the native approvals themselves (W2R)
31. Way 2 continues from your framework's own checkpoint
32. Way 2 keeps your framework's checkpoint (the artifacts API by hand)
33. by design: outside a harness run your code names the key of its own write; the runs SDK and the memory SDK take idempotency_key=
34. a block runs inline in your code: no surface or queue of its own here
35. by design: your code calls another agent with remote() (A2A), or runs it as plain code
36. your framework runs its calls
37. by design: a Way 2 caller's own code receives the whole result and decides what its model reads
38. native middleware: a graph is built with it
39. checked by F41
40. by design: agent_tools() returns JSON-schema tool specs every framework takes as they are, and call_agent_tool() runs them
41. by design: memory.tool_hints() ranks the tools; your code offers the ones it picks
42. Way 2 lists a server's tools with the MCP SDK itself, then calls them as tools
43. Code Mode is the gateway's: Way 2 calls its meta-tools through bifrost-sdk
44. by design: your code reads the prompt from Bifrost's prompt repository itself (h.prompt is the Way 1 form)
45. by design: OpenTelemetry is the block: your code's own spans, which the SDKs continue (traceparent)
46. Way 1 only by design (README: surfaces are the harness's)
47. RunStart.agent_version: your code sets it
48. no run of the harness's in Way 2: your code has its own
49. RunStart.timeout_seconds: your code sets it (F09's Way 2 row)
50. RunStart/ScheduleSpec.priority: your code sets it (F09's Way 2 row)
51. Way 2 selects by import
52. Way 2 calls the framework itself, with its own options
53. sandbox tools are harness tools: they run in a harness run (Way 1, with blocks)
54. Way 2 selects by import: each block is used or not by your own code
55. probed in Way 1; the plan names no Way 2 form yet
